question: Rising prices are affecting households and businesses across the European Union, with the cost of energy and essential goods soaring to unprecedented levels1. Greece is among the countries with the highest prices, which are worsening social inequalities and threatening the country’s economic recovery. Addressing the issue of rising prices is crucial and requires immediate and effective action at the EU level. 1.
How does the Commission intend to address the unprecedented rise in the prices of energy and essential goods?
Does the Commission plan to create a European price observatory to monitor the market, identify profiteering and ensure healthy competition?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (14.6.2024) In May 2022 the Commission adopted the REPowerEU plan in response the unprecedented rise in energy prices resulting from the Russian invasion of Ukraine. The Commission recently published a web-based report taking stock of the progress made since the adoption of REPowerEU1 and set out recommendations and guidance documents.

Furthermore, to fortify resilience against high, volatile prices and draw on lessons from the energy crisis, the EU has recently adopted the electricity market reform. This reform will help to make the market future-proof to maximise the benefits of affordable clean energy, better protect EU consumers and empower them in the green energy transition. The Commission is committed to its effective implementation.

The EU also recently adopted the Hydrogen and decarbonised gas market package. Effective implementation of the new retail market rules therein will empower customers to save money and benefit from renewable and low-carbon energy, as well as better protect them from disconnection. Those in energy poverty are most hit by rising prices.

This is one of the reasons that last year the Commission adopted a Recommendation on energy poverty2 which sets out measures and policies that can be adopted by Member States. The Commission produces quarterly reports on EU gas and electricity wholesale and retail markets. This can be found on the Commission website3.

Progress reports on the internal market in electricity and the internal market in natural gas are also published as part of the State of the Energy Union report in accordance with the Regulation (EU) 2018/1999 on the Governance of the Energy Union and Climate Action4.
